service.description: The sprints of a project: the open ones (in progress first, then the planned by start) and, with includeClosed, the completed ones (the latest first), each with its dates as text, goal, capacity and status label; none for a user who does not see the project or is a client contact (impl-projects.md F111).

The Backlog screen's data for a project the user sees: the project (key, name, estimate unit, whether it plans in sprints (WstModules backlog), runs several sprints at once, and what the user may do), the backlog rows and each open sprint with its rows, item count, total size against its capacity; and the filter options. The filters (assignee, type, label, component, epic: under a top-level item at any depth, and text) narrow the rows of both panes, not a sprint's total. Each row is as WorkItems decorates it, with its epic (its top-level item) and its size in the project's unit.

A drag in the Backlog: the items (workEffortIds, in their order) go to the sprint sprintWorkEffortId (empty for the backlog) and, in that list, right after previousWorkEffortId, else before nextWorkEffortId, one after the other (set#TaskSprint, set#TaskBacklogRank); with neither (an empty list) only the sprint changes. Each item on its own, in its own transaction, by one who may change it: one that fails is logged and named, the rest go on.
One item of rank#BacklogItems: its sprint when it changes, then its rank.

A sprint and its project's access (get#ProjectAccess with need): sprint (the record), project, canView, canUpdate (the team: rank, plan, edit, start, complete), canManage. A sprint the user may not see is "not available".

SprintForm: a new sprint of the project (no workEffortId; mantle create#Sprint) or the changes to one (update#Sprint): name, goal, start and end (yyyy-MM-dd), capacity in the project's unit. By the project's team.
StartSprint: begins a planned sprint with its dates and goal (mantle start#Sprint, which refuses while another is in progress unless the project allows several, naming it). By the project's team.
CompleteSprint: ends a sprint in progress (mantle complete#Sprint); its open items go to carryToSprintId, else by carryTo (next, new or backlog). By the project's team.
"Plan in sprints": turns the Backlog and sprints module on for the project (WstModules backlog), by one who manages it.

The open sprints of a project (in progress, then planned) as drop-down options (key, text) for the sprint fields of quick add, QuickWorkItem, WorkItemDetail and the bulk change; none for a project the user does not see.

SprintDetail's data: the sprint (name, goal, dates, capacity, status and its label), its project, what the user may do, the numbers (committed, completed, remaining, days left) and burndown by day, the scope changes and the items with what became of each (mantle.work.ProjectReportServices.get#SprintBurndown), the item rows as WorkItems decorates them, and for Complete the counts and the open sprints the open items may go to.
A milestone or release and its project's access (get#ProjectAccess with need): plan (the record), project, canView, canUpdate (the team), canManage. One the user may not see is "not available".

parameter.name: kind
parameter.description: milestone or release: only that kind

service.description: Milestones, releases and sprints as the Roadmap shows them: the kind with its label and icon, the project, the start and due as text and as days, the status (label, color), whether it is open or overdue, the progress (done of the items, hours; mantle get#PlanItemSummary), the date it was reached or released, its detail's link and whether the user may change it (the project's team).

NewMilestone, NewRelease and the Edit of MilestoneDetail and ReleaseDetail: a new milestone or release of rootWorkEffortId (kind milestone or release, no workEffortId: mantle create#Milestone, create#Release; the id given or the next KEY-MS-n or KEY-REL-n) or the changes to one (update#Milestone): name (a release's version), description, start and due (yyyy-MM-dd; empty clears them on an edit), status. By the project's team.
The statuses a milestone or release may move to from its own by the Default flow (the in-place edit and the status menu), with its own first: [{value, label}].
One field of a milestone or release from the Roadmap's in-place edits: due (yyyy-MM-dd, empty clears) or status (along the Default flow). By the project's team. valueText is the field's new text.

MilestoneDetail's and ReleaseDetail's data: the plan item (name, description, dates, status and its label, the stages of the Default flow and the moves from its status), its project, what the user may do, the progress (decorate#PlanItemRows: items by state, hours and points), the items as WorkItems shows them (find#WorkItems with the milestone or release, so only the items the user may see) with the state of each (notStarted, inProgress, done, cancelled) and, for a release, the group (Features, Fixes, Other), the other open milestones or releases of the project (where unfinished items may go).

Add items: the work items of the plan item's project the user may see that are not in it, by key or words (find#WorkItems with the text), open ones first, as drop-down options [{value, label}], up to 20.

Puts work items (workEffortIds, a list or comma text) in a milestone or release (remove: takes them out), each on its own (mantle.work.TaskServices.set#TaskPlanItem, which refuses an item of another project); one that fails is logged and named, the others go on. By the project's team.

Move unfinished items: a milestone's or release's items not done (not Complete, Closed or Cancelled) to another open one of the project (toWorkEffortId) or out of it (empty), each on its own. By the project's team.

ReleaseDetail's code, of the repositories the user may view (org.moqui.git.GitServices.get#GitRepositoryAccess): the merge requests of its items (WorkEffortGitMergeRequest; merged ones first, then open, with !num, title, status and when merged), its tags (WorkEffortGitRef of the release, refType tag), the project's repositories the user may update (to make a tag at their default branch, or a ref given) and the tags of the project's repositories not linked yet (to link one). Without git hosting in the build, hosting is false and the rest empty; a part that fails is logged and left empty.

ReleaseTag's Create tag: an annotated tag (tagName, by default v and the version) at revision (the default branch's head when empty) in repositoryId, a repository of the release's project (org.moqui.git.GitServices.create#GitRef, which checks the right to create and the branch rules), linked to the release. By the project's team.

ReleaseNotes' data: the notes as kept (mantle get#ReleaseNotes), else a generated draft (generate#ReleaseNotes, draft true), when they were saved, the page they are published as (with its link, when the user may view it), and whether the project has a documentation space. A client contact gets the published notes only.

ReleaseNotes' Save (the text as written), Generate draft (generate: the notes made again from the items and merge requests, replacing the text) and Publish (publish: the notes as written, to the docs space when toDocs, CHANGELOG.md of repositoryId when toChangelog, the followers when notify; mantle publish#ReleaseNotes, each way on its own). By the project's team.

ReleaseDetail's Release: mantle release#Release for the project's team (the items not done to moveUnfinishedTo, Complete today, a tag when createTag, the notes published when publish). Its warnings stay as messages.

The Timeline's data in one of three modes: - items (the default): the work items of the find (ironstone.projects.WorkItemServices.find#WorkItems: list, all by default with the cancelled ones left out, text, type, assignee, sprint, milestone, release, label; one project with rootWorkEffortId), up to 500, with their ancestors (mantle.work.ProjectServices.get#TimelineData) so the tree holds them: each row as WorkItems decorates it, with its own start and due, a parent's span over its sub-items, progress, depth and whether the user may move it; the dependencies between them (kept or broken); the projects' milestones, releases and sprints (decorate#PlanItemRows) and the holidays of their organizations. - plan (the Roadmap's timeline view): the milestones, releases and, in one project, sprints, as bars or markers (find#RoadmapItems with planList, all by default). - portfolio (the Projects list's timeline view): the projects of the find (ironstone.projects.ProjectServices.find#Projects with projectList, active by default) as bars from their start to their due (else the span of their items), each with its open milestones and releases as markers. Who sees a project sees its timeline; its team (canUpdate) moves bars and makes dependencies. A project given that the user may not see is notAvailable.

A drag on the Timeline: a work item's, milestone's or release's start and due (yyyy-MM-dd; an empty text clears one, a parameter not given leaves it) by the project's team (mantle.work.TaskServices.set#TaskDates); a parent's summary bar takes its sub-items along (moveSubtree), and with autoSchedule the items that depend on it move on by business days. The message names how many items moved and those that could not.

parameter.name: shiftDays
parameter.description: A bar dragged along: its dates by that many days

service.description: DependencyForm and a drag from a bar's end to another bar: workEffortId waits for toWorkEffortId with lagDays working days (mantle.work.TaskServices.add#TaskDependency: a loop, its own branch of the tree or a negative lag refused), by one who may change workEffortId and sees toWorkEffortId.
DependencyForm's Remove: workEffortId no longer waits for toWorkEffortId (mantle remove#TaskDependency), by one who may change workEffortId.

actions.script: ec.service.sync().name('ironstone.commons.TaskServices.get#TaskAccess').parameters({workEffortId: workEffortId, need: 'update', app: 'projects'}).call() if (ec.message.hasError()) return ec.service.sync().name('mantle.work.TaskServices.remove#TaskDependency').parameters({workEffortId: workEffortId, toWorkEffortId: toWorkEffortId}).call() if (ec.message.hasError()) return message = ec.resource.expand(ec.l10n.localize('${id} no longer waits for ${to}'), '', {id: workEffortId, to: toWorkEffortId})

service.description: The project's calendar (design-projects.md §4 ProjectCalendar: Commons Calendar.qvue in its project mode) from start to end (days yyyy-MM-dd in the user's time zone), as Calendar.qvue takes events: the meetings linked to the project (mantle.work.EventServices.get#FullCalendarData rootWorkEffortId, recurring ones expanded), its sprints over their days, its milestones and releases on their due days (a phase's start a day of its own, not moved), and its work items by their due day (ironstone.projects.WorkItemServices.find#WorkItems, so a Restricted item only for those who see it). A milestone, release or work item the user may change moves by a drag (movable). Each part on its own: one that fails is logged and named in failedSources.

A drag in the project's calendar (start, yyyy-MM-dd, the day it was dropped on): a work item's due day moves; a milestone or release moves by as many days as its due day did, its start with it so a phase keeps its length (move#TimelineItem).

MilestoneDetail's Gate, Billing and Deliverables (design-projects.md §4 MilestoneGate, MilestoneBillingShare, Deliverables): the gate (mantle.work.ProjectServices.get#MilestoneApprovalAccess: required, the approver, the latest request with its texts, the requests before it, what the user may do: ask, decide (for the approver: recorded for them), set the gate) and the people who may approve (the project's managers and client contacts); for one who manages money the billing shares (get#MilestoneBilling: order line, percent, amount, billed or due) and the project's order lines to add one to; the deliverables (WorkEffortDeliverableProd and Deliverable: name, type, description, accepted when and by whom). For one who sees the milestone; else extras is null.

MilestoneDetail's gate actions (mantle.work.ProjectServices): gate (set whether approval is needed and the approver; store#MilestoneGate), request (request#MilestoneApproval with comments), approve (approve#MilestoneApproval: by the approver, or recorded for them by one who manages the project; the milestone is reached), refuse (refuse#MilestoneApproval with the reason), cancel (cancel#MilestoneApproval). The checks are Mantle's.

A deliverable of a milestone (design-projects.md §4 Deliverables): a new one (Deliverable and WorkEffortDeliverableProd, last in order) or the name, type and description of one; by the project's team.

A milestone's deliverable accepted (or not, with accept N) by one who decides the milestone's gate (its approver, or one who manages the project for them), or taken off the milestone (remove, by the project's team; not once accepted).
